business_scope.primary_industry_name: Accounts Receivable Factoring and Cross-Border Reverse Factoring

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid jurisdiction: French-inspired civil law system, with Article 2 of the Egyptian Constitution establishing Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation; company law, commercial registration, and non-bank financial regulation (CBE/FRA) operate as a unitary national regime without sub-state tax distinction.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1982, entered into force 1992)
Egypt-Germany Bilateral Investment Treaty (amended and renewed 2007)
EU-Egypt Association Agreement (2004) with establishment and capital liberalization provisions
Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital in the Arab States (1980)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering (as amended notably by Law No. 36 of 2014), its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2003, as amended), and the directives of the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU); Law No. 4 of 2018 on Companies (beneficial ownership register and incorporation requirements); Law No. 72 of 2017 on Investment; Law No. 10 of 2009 on Regulation of Non-Banking Financial Markets and Instruments (FRA licensing of factoring activities); Central Bank of Egypt AML circulars; FRA licensing rules for factoring companies.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — UBO declarations are filed with GAFI/Companies Registry and the Commercial Registry, and are made available to EMLCU, CBE, FRA, and prosecutorial authorities; UBO data is not accessible through public commercial-registry search.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; require origin-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization followed by Egyptian Embassy/Consulate authentication)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: General Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian resident counsel/incorporation agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or issuing passport authority of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration and AML/CFT questionnaire of all direct and indirect shareholders

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds documentation for the equity injection
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank of the transferring account

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD/EDD under Law 80 of 2002 and EMLCU regulations before authorization: all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, affiliated financing parties, and counterpart banks must be screened against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions, UK HMT sanctions, the Egyptian EMLCU domestic terrorist-financing list, and Arab League sanctions. PEP status, as defined by FATF, triggers senior-management approval and enhanced monitoring; all screening evidence and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds documentation must be retained for FRA inspection during the factoring license review.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Electronic Company Registration and Name Clearance Portal operated by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI / www.gafi.gov.eg), in coordination with the Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory name applications must be submitted in Modern Standard Arabic; the official corporate name is Arabic with an optional Latin transliteration appearing as a secondary registered translation. The Arabic name must be phonetically distinct from existing registered names; transliteration follows standard Arabic orthography rules applied by GAFI; a Latin-only name is not acceptable as the legal corporate designation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Finance (Tamweel) - restricted for non-licensed trade-finance entities
Factoring (Al-Takseem) - requires prior FRA non-bank financial license
National (Qawmi/Watani), Government, Presidential, or sovereign references
Arab (Al-'Arabi) or Misr (Egypt) - requires GAFI special authorization
United Nations, World Bank, IMF, GAFI, or other intergovernmental names
Military, Intelligence, Police, or sovereign-security references
Words contrary to public order, religious symbols, or public morality
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the GAFI portal issues an electronic refusal citing the conflicting or prohibited token. The applicant may (i) correct the name and re-file, or (ii) submit a formal administrative grievance to the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 15 working days of the refusal, attaching a comparative list of existing names. A second adverse decision may be challenged before the Egyptian State Council (administrative justice) under Law No. 136 of 1984, with annulment filing required within 60 days of the final administrative decision; local counsel representation is mandatory. Name clearance certificates are valid for 90 days, renewable upon updated re-application prior to incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the licensed factoring operation: the FRA requires a physical registered office in Egypt with lease or ownership proof, visible signage, dedicated AML/CFT record storage, and resident compliance personnel; a virtual-office address alone will not satisfy FRA licensing, CBE wire/escrow account opening, or commercial-registry inspection requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High and quantified: 75% estimated probability of an unannounced FRA on-site AML/CFT inspection within the first 12 months of licensed operations; 90-95% probability of inspection before license renewal; elevated joint CBE/EMLCU inspection risk given cross-border Swift-wire and reverse-factoring flows.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018), Articles 1-8 and 22-73 governing limited liability companies; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations for investor facilitation and one-stop-shop procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration & Commercial Registry One-Stop Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association in Arabic, filed electronically through GAFI's investor registration system and notarized as required.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for an LLC; the founding shareholders must determine the capital in the Incorporation Contract, fully subscribe it, and may pay it in cash or kind. No escrow account is mandated for LLC formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution of [Company] LLC, adopted unanimously by the founding shareholders on [Date]. RESOLVED: (1) that the subscription for 100% of the share capital be accepted and issued as stated in the Incorporation Contract; (2) that the premises at [Registered Address], Egypt, be adopted as the registered office and principal business place; (3) that the managers named in the Register of Managers be appointed for the first fiscal year, with authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and represent the company before GAFI, the Financial Regulatory Authority, and tax authorities; (4) that the shareholders be empowered to complete filings and remit registration fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Activity Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI e-Services Portal at www.gafi.gov.eg / Central Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit 2-3 proposed Arabic names with the Latin transliteration, the intended Egyptian limited liability company activity, and the ISIC scope. GAFI screens for similarity, conflict, and public policy compliance. After a successful preliminary check, obtain a name reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Copy of each founding shareholder's national ID or passport
Proposed company name list (Arabic and Latin)
Short description of the factoring and trade supply chain finance activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit alternative names within 5 working days through the same portal; only names conflicting with protected sovereign or religious designations are final.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Incorporation Contract and Capital Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI one-stop-shop notaries / official Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Incorporation Contract before the competent notary or through GAFI's recognized electronic signature. Verify that the LLC capital is allocated among shareholders; for commercial registration, the contract must identify the registered office, managers, and first fiscal year. Rent the registered office prior to notarization.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate from GAFI
Valid passports or national IDs of all founding shareholders
Lease agreement or title deed for the proposed registered office in Egypt
Draft Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association
Consent declarations from the appointed managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags an irregularity, correct the capital clause or management appointments and re-execute within 10 working days; no public notarial fee refund applies after execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and GAFI Company File Creation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (Madinat Nasr or relevant governorate branch)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Incorporation Contract, manager appointments, registered office proof, and all statutory forms to GAFI. GAFI reviews compliance with Companies Law and upon approval assigns a commercial registration number, files the company, and uploads the certificate of incorporation to its electronic system.
required_dossiers: Notarized Incorporation Contract in Arabic
Name reservation certificate
Manager identity documents and appointment consents
Certificate proving the registered office address
Stamp duty payment receipt
Companies Law compliance forms issued by GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query, respond within 15 working days to the responsible examiner; minor defects may be corrected by submitting a complementary memorandum rather than a full re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - e-Tax services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the commercial registration number, register the LLC with the ETA for income tax and VAT if taxable activities exceed the VAT compulsory threshold. File the company data, manager details, registered office, and banking information; obtain the tax card and electronic tax ID.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate from GAFI
Notarized Incorporation Contract
Tax representative appointment letter / board resolution
Manager national ID or passport copy
Registered office lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA requires clarification, submit the missing accounting records or lease documents within 10 working days; ETA objections are handled through the ETA internal review window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) - local social insurance office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with NOSI as an employer, submit the list of managers and initial employees (if any), and obtain the social insurance file number. The incorporation contract and commercial registration certificate are required.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate
Tax card
Incorporation Contract
Manager and employee identity documents
Employment contracts or appointment letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI rejects due to incomplete data, correct the employment records and re-submit the file within 5 working days; social insurance is registered retroactively to the appointment date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) - Non-Banking Financial Activity Oversight Sector
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factoring License issued under the Factoring Regulation Law No. 176 of 2018 and FRA executive regulations for accounts receivable factoring and reverse factoring activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D: Exempt - non-industrial commercial office; a self-declaration of environmental registration is retained in the company file.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater limited to domestic sanitary discharge into municipal sewers within the standards of Law No. 4 of 1994; no industrial process, VOC-emitting equipment, or combustion emissions on site; e-waste and confidential records disposal must be contracted with an EEAA-licensed waste management operator.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the General Department of Civil Defense; structural load inspection certificate issued by an accredited engineering office for the registered office premises; and workplace safety clearance from the Ministry of Manpower confirming occupational safety and health compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance — official national portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipt platform: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg; customs single window (NAFEZA) administered by the Egyptian Customs Authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Secure the FRA factoring licence (Law 176/2018) as a precondition for tax registration. Step 2 — Notarize the LLC’s memorandum of association and complete Commercial Registry filing; obtain the start-up certificate (I'jazah Ebteda'eyah). Step 3 — Submit the CR certificate, FRA licence, lease/title evidence of the head office, manager/shareholder IDs and foreign-ownership documents to the competent ETA office; receive the company file and the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and tax card. Step 4 — Complete VAT registration at the same ETA office once taxable supplies reach EGP 500,000 (mandatory threshold) or elect voluntary registration at EGP 50,000; obtain the VAT number. Step 5 — Register on the ETA e-invoicing portal, complete API integration and pass the sandbox validation tests to obtain the production UUID. Step 6 — Open the Egyptian bank account at a CBE-licensed bank and register as an exporter in the NAFEZA system to obtain the customs exporter code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Egyptian LLC is an opaque resident taxpayer under Income Tax Law 91/2005: worldwide net income is taxed at 22.5% CIT; no pass-through or fiscal-transparency treatment is permitted; profit distributions attract 10% dividend WHT; a non-resident shareholder may claim treaty relief under Egypt’s double taxation treaties. Territorial relief applies only to foreign branch profits under the conditions of Article 39 of Law 91/2005.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Egyptian law; classification is prescribed by legal form. Available mechanisms: (i) free-zone regime election under Investment Law 72/2017 for ETA/Zone-approved entities (practically unavailable for financial services unless integrated with a SCZONE licence); (ii) voluntary VAT registration; (iii) advance pricing agreements and transfer-pricing documentation elections under Executive Regulations 991/2016; (iv) foreign tax credit election for limited foreign-branch profits; (v) thin-capitalization compliance (4:1 debt-to-equity on shareholder loans) to protect interest deductibility; (vi) hybrid-mismatch documentation to safeguard deduction/credit symmetry.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Law No. 67 of 2016 (as amended by Law 3/2021 and the 2025 rate amendment) and its Executive Regulations; the standard rate was 13% on enactment, 14% from 1 July 2017, and 15% from 1 July 2025; certain schedule-listed goods and services carry reduced rates.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable turnover (mandatory registration) and EGP 50,000 (voluntary registration); the threshold is applied to the entity as a whole, and no invoice may be issued without prior VAT registration once the threshold is met.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory end-to-end e-invoicing for all VAT-registered businesses (phased since 2021 with full coverage of registered taxpayers by 2024). B2B/B2G e-invoices in XML are transmitted in real time (within 24 hours of issuance) via the ETA API for validation, digital stamping and issuance of a unique UUID before the invoice is legally issued; the B2C e-receipt regime has been mandatory for retailers since April 2022. Non-compliance attracts fines of EGP 20,000–EGP 100,000 per invoice and disallowance of input VAT credits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of tangible goods carried out of Egypt is zero-rated under the VAT law upon proof of customs exit, contract, commercial invoice, B/L/AWB and inward FX remittance. Services qualify for zero-rating only where the place of supply is outside Egypt and the benefit is effectively consumed abroad; for cross-border trade factoring, the financing spread falls under the financial-services exemption, while separately itemized factoring/administration fees are taxable at 15% but may be zero-rated for a non-resident debtor when supported by the factoring agreement, foreign-currency invoice and bank FX receipt. The ETA should be asked for an advance ruling on the fee/discount split before issuing the first zero-rated invoice.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed via NAFEZA single window
Commercial Invoice (matching the ETA-validated e-invoice UUID)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank FX receipt of the export price)
Export/factoring contract evidencing the foreign-debtor receivable
ETA e-invoice validation report and export statement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA refund audits cross-match customs declarations, shipping records and bank FX receipts through NAFEZA and CBE systems. False zero-rating or overclaimed refunds trigger: (i) clawback with legal-penalty interest at 1.5% per month plus the CBE discount rate; (ii) administrative fines under Law 67/2016; (iii) criminal tax-evasion penalties of EGP 50,000–EGP 10,000,000 and imprisonment of 2–5 years under Law 206/2020 and Article 66 of Law 67/2016; (iv) suspension of the export refund certificate for up to one year. Export proceeds not repatriated within 90 days are further scrutinized under CBE exchange-control rules and may lead to reclassification of the revenue as taxable in Egypt.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) is the sole monetary, banking and foreign exchange supervisory authority in Egypt, operating under the Banking Law No. 194 of 2020. The CBE exercises Exchange Control through its Upper Committee for Foreign Exchange Policy, the General Department for Banking Supervision, and the Foreign Exchange Operations Department. The Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) independently licenses and supervises non-bank financial activities, including factoring and trade receivables securitization, while the CBE retains mandatory registration, repatriation, and monitoring powers over all cross-border currency flows affecting Egyptian legal entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since March 2024, the CBE abolished the administrative exchange-rate peg and implemented a flexible exchange-rate regime under which the EGP/USD rate is determined by interbank supply and demand through authorized banks. Current-account transactions, including trade payments, service fees, factoring collections, and genuine commercial remittances, are broadly convertible without prior CBE approval provided the underlying transaction has complete commercial documentation and is routed through an authorized Egyptian bank. Capital-account transactions, namely foreign share-capital injections, shareholder loans, and portfolio inflows, are subject to mandatory inflow registration with the CBE and the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI). Profit and dividend repatriation by a non-resident shareholder is legally permitted but practically gated by the following hurdles: (i) audited financial statements for the distributable period; (ii) a signed board resolution authorizing the dividend; (iii) a valid tax card and a tax clearance certificate from the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); (iv) an approved foreign-currency transfer request lodged through the corporate account-holding bank; and (v) the bank's independent KYC verification of the receiving beneficial owner, with no available offshore EGP clearing. There is no statutory percentage cap on dividend remittance, but a foreign shareholder must prove the source of the invested funds at onboarding or the remittance is treated as a portfolio exit requiring additional CBE approval. Non-resident factoring counterparties cannot hold EGP balances outside Egypt. In practice, all EGP conversion for the LLC must be executed physically inside Egypt via a Tier-1 authorized bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBE export and banking circulars applicable to Egyptian exporters: (a) all export shipments must be documented and financed through an authorized bank, with the bill of lading, commercial invoice, and certificate of origin lodged with the bank; (b) export proceeds in a CBE-acceptable foreign currency must be credited to the exporter's account in Egypt within 180 days from the date of the bill of lading / airway bill or from the date of the underlying export invoice for services; the exporter's bank can grant a one-time extension of up to a further 180 days upon a documented justification; (c) the applicable mandatory conversion ratio into EGP is currently 0% — Egypt has abolished statutory surrender requirements, and the exporter may retain 100% of export receipts in a Special Foreign Currency Account for approved trade and treasury purposes; (d) notwithstanding the 0% conversion ratio, the CBE has a discretionary statutory power to impose a temporary surrender ratio under emergency balance-of-payments conditions, so the treasury blueprint must preserve full traceability of export receipts and avoid commingling with local EGP collections; (e) the exporter must match each export bill with its corresponding foreign-currency receipt, a process called 'export bill matching', and residues or discrepancies trigger automatic enhanced reporting; (f) for the EG_LLC factoring platform, when the company legally purchases export receivables it assumes the exporter's repatriation obligation, therefore a true-sale assignment must transfer the original export documentation bundle to the LLC and the debtor remittances must flow back to the LLC's Egyptian foreign-currency account within the 180-day window; (g) for reverse factoring of Egyptian importers, the outbound disbursement to a non-resident supplier is classified as an import payment and requires the import-purpose code and the related CBE import-monitoring registration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: EGP Operational Current Account + USD Special Foreign Currency Account + Trade Escrow Sub-Account
EGP Operational Account + Foreign Currency Settlement Account with dedicated export-proceeds ledger
EGP Operational Account + USD Cross-Border Account with SWIFT correspondent clearing and mandated escrow overlay
Export-Focused Factoring Collection Account + USD Escrow Account under the FRA-financed trade framework
EGP Operational Account + USD Settlement Account with regional correspondent reach
EGP Operational Account + Global USD Clearing Account linked to HSBC London network

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM with material legal constraints. The CBE does not recognize or passport foreign Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and does not permit non-resident fintech firms to hold EGP balances, issue EGP-denominated accounts, or clear EGP-denominated payments inside Egypt. Offshore digital banking platforms such as Wise, Payoneer, Stripe, or EU/UK-licensed EMIs can be used only as supplementary foreign-currency collection gateways for small ticket receivables and must in every case be followed by a formal SWIFT MT103 settlement into a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank account; routing the initial capital injection or factoring facility proceeds through an external EMI without an Egyptian licensed banking 'point of conversion' is not AML-compliant and would be classified as a third-party suspicious remittance. A CBE-licensed local bank is therefore the exclusive primary clearing rail; a fintech sandbox entrant registered with the CBE and FRA can be used abroad only as a technology orchestrator, never as the principal payment settlement institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the first corporate account activation under CBE Know-Your-Customer rules. The legal representative, the general manager, and any shareholder holding 25% or more of the EG_LLC equity must attend an in-person interview at the Egyptian bank branch with original passports or Egyptian national IDs; the CBE does not currently allow a fully remote onboarding path for a first-time Egyptian corporate account. After the physical interview, banks may apply remote video verification for subsequent signatory updates and ongoing treasury operations. All corporate documents lodged by a foreign beneficial owner require legalization or apostille in accordance with the Hague Convention and certified Arabic translation. Any attempt to open the account without at least one director physically present in Egypt is consistently rejected by NBE, Banque Misr, and CIB; the remote-only onboarding viability tier is therefore Low.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership mismatch — the declared UBO over 25% as described in the banking application differs from the shareholding structure recorded in the Commercial Registry and in the GAFI investment certificate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated Commercial Registry extract not older than three months; notarized LLC Articles of Association; share register and transfer ledger; signed CBE Beneficial Ownership Declaration Form; passport/national ID copies of all shareholders in the ownership chain; a written ownership reconciliation memo supported by an Egyptian corporate lawyer's opinion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds inadequacy for the initial capital injection and escrow top-up — the bank flags that the incoming wired amount originates from a third-party remitter rather than the exact foreign shareholder named in the subscription resolution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of certified bank statements of the contributing shareholder; executed share-subscription resolution; GAFI foreign-investment certificate; capital-contribution KYC declaration; a notarized explanation of the payment-chain reason where a bridge lender or group treasury executed the remittance on behalf of the shareholder; a signed statement of the ultimate economic source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected unlicensed credit collection — the bank questions whether the account supports genuine factoring or a disguised lending business requiring a separate FRA license for non-bank lending.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FRA factoring license issued to EG_LLC for the trade-supply-chain factoring scope; fully executed true-sale factoring agreements with assignment notices; a legal opinion confirming that the ownership of receivables passes to the factor and that the activity is a licensed financial lease/assignment and not prohibited lending; the company's AML/CFT compliance manual approved by the appointed compliance officer; evidence of FRA reporting of factoring volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore collection pattern without repatriation — the bank suspects that factoring collections are settled to an overseas trust or escrow rather than back to the Egyptian banking system, thereby circumventing CBE export-proceeds repatriation rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aged receivable ledger with each debtor's remittance reference; every export bill or supply invoice matched to an MT103 credit into the Egyptian USD account; a treasury policy statement committing to 100% onshore collection within the 180-day statutory window; NAFEZA customs export verification reports; an external auditor's certification that all collections are reconciled and repatriated; a signed compliance undertaking to the CBE on the movement of trade proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person (PEP) flag connected to a director, beneficial owner, or a major counterparty supplier.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed commercial-screen PEP report produced by an Egpyt-registered screening provider; completed CBE/PEP enhanced due-diligence questionnaire; notarized declarations of the PEP status and the nature of the relationship; evidence of the person's legitimate income and tax settlement; a formal enhanced-monitoring plan accepted by the bank's AML officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-pattern mismatch — the account shows rapid in-and-out wiring inconsistent with the declared trade-factoring business scope, triggering CBE circular reports on suspicious structural transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Factoring pipeline contracts with non-resident corporates; underlying purchase orders and invoices in English/Arabic; debtor instruction letters authorizing payment routing; a transaction-by-transaction reconciliation approved by the external auditor; a board-approved treasury policy describing the matching of each inbound factoring fund with an outbound supplier disbursement; a demonstrated liquidity-netting control consistent with the Stage-8 compliance architecture.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant protocol requires the foreign shareholder to originate an SWIFT MT103 using the exact remitter account declared in the GAFI/CBE registration; the narrative field must read 'Capital Increase — EG_LLC — Trade & Supply Chain Factoring — ISIC 6492' and the wire must be routed directly to the EG_LLC escrow or USD operating account held at the Egyptian Tier-1 bank, with a fallback route through the Egyptian bank's nostro account for jurisdictions with correspondent restrictions. The receiving bank will pause the credit pending submission of the incorporation deed, Commercial Registry extract, GAFI certificate, tax card, account-operation authorization resolution, and beneficiary ownership declaration, after which the bank issues the foreign-direct-investment inflow registration with the CBE. The applicable Egyptian banking purpose code for the inflow is the investment/capital-subscription code, not a trade-fees code; using a service-fee purpose code would trigger reclassification and penalty risk. The escrow sub-ledger must remain dormant until the full compliance file is cleared, and all inbound FX proceeds must be converted to EGP only through the authorized bank's dealing desk to establish an orderly transaction audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recommended clearing rails in order of preference: (A) SWIFT MT103 single client credit transfer for supplier and reverse-factoring beneficiary payments, executed only when the invoice and beneficiary details match the Egyptian bank's static data and the amount is within the approved CBE threshold; (B) SWIFT MT202 COV for correspondent-to-correspondent clearing when a beneficiary bank rejects MT103 on EGP restrictions or when the transaction is settled via a shared nostro in New York, London, or Frankfurt; (C) Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary LC, governed by UCP600) for high-value inbound raw-material purchases, opened through the Egyptian bank's SWIFT infrastructure and supported by the CBE import-monitoring unit registration; (D) factoring settlement dispersals to Egyptian suppliers require proof that the underlying receivable has been registered in the CBE/FRA database and that collection of the assigned invoice has actually occurred before the outflow is executed; (E) cross-border cash-pooling and zero-balancing structures require prior written CBE approval and are not assumed as a default legal right. Every outbound wire must carry in MT103 field 59 the exact registered name of the Egyptian operating entity, and the funding account in field 50F must match the cleared CBE account, because any name mismatch is the leading cause of bank freezing, delayed clearing, and AML suspension in the Egyptian correspondent banking network.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) executed with an authorized Egyptian bank against a genuine underlying trade, factoring, or investment exposure, with a documented one-to-one cover ratio and automatic CBE operational reporting through the executing bank.

Offshore EGP non-deliverable forwards (EGP NDFs) quoted in London and New York for the non-resident counterparty only; the Egyptian-resident EG_LLC cannot directly enter an offshore NDF and must hedge onshore through its licensed Egyptian bank's book.

Deliverable foreign-currency swaps (USD/EGP principal exchange and interest-rate exchange) with an onshore authorized commercial bank, approved solely when a documented capital or trade cash-flow exists and speculative swap positions are prohibited.

Short-term FX swap facilities offered by the CBE to local banks for domestic liquidity smoothing; the LLC participates only as a bank client within the commercial bank's authorized swap framework, never as a direct CBE counterparty.

Plain vanilla foreign-currency options are generally not available to non-bank Egyptian corporates and require express CBE Monetary Operations Division authorization; reliance on options cannot be assumed without a confirmed local bank product approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form No. 115) for the LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Corporate Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than April 30 following the calendar fiscal year-end, i.e. within four months from the end of the tax period under the income tax procedural rules of Law No. 30 of 2023
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty escalating from EGP 5,000 (~USD 100) to EGP 50,000 (~USD 1,000) for unreasonably delayed submissions under Law No. 30 of 2023; additional monthly delayed-tax interest of 3% on unpaid corporate tax; prolonged non-filing triggers enforced collection against bank accounts and movable assets but does not itself commence administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements and FRA annual compliance return for the factoring license under Law No. 176 of 2018
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), Non-Banking Financial Services Supervision Sector
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days of the December 31 fiscal year-end, normally March 30; FRA licensing decree may also require an interim 6-month compliance filing by August 31 for active reverse-factoring portfolios
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: FRA administrative fine up to EGP 200,000 (~USD 4,000) plus daily penalty accrual; chronic non-filing warrants suspension or revocation of the factoring license; license revocation mandates solvent winding-up of the LLC and immediate cessation of escrow and Swift-wire receivables settlement activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry data confirmation and renewal of the commercial register extract
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry, via the GAFI one-stop desk for GAFI-registered LLCs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual registry data confirmation must be lodged in January of each year; the commercial registration record undergoes full renewal on the 5th anniversary of initial registration; any change in managers, registered office, corporate purpose, or capital must be filed within 15 days of the occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal penalty of EGP 500 (~USD 10) for the first month and EGP 1,000 (~USD 20) for each subsequent month of delinquency; failure to maintain valid commercial registration exposes the LLC to administrative deletion from the Commercial Registry (strike-off), judicial closure of operations, and loss of legal capacity to issue invoices or enforce factoring assignments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and AML register confirmation statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and the Commercial Registry under Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended by Law No. 169 of 2021 and the FRA factoring rule-book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO register must be updated and annually confirmed no later than January 31; any shareholding transfer must be reflected in the UBO register and notified to the Commercial Registry and FRA within 15 days of the transfer effective date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML non-compliance penalties ranging from EGP 50,000 (~USD 1,000) to EGP 200,000 (~USD 4,000) under Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended; failure to maintain accurate UBO records additionally exposes the factoring license to FRA suspension because of elevated financial-crime risk classification; administrative strike-off is not the direct remedy, but license revocation becomes a realistic supervisory outcome for repeat delinquencies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for every Egyptian LLC: the General Assembly must appoint at least one certified auditor under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981. For an ISIC 6492 factoring licensee, FRA supervision under Law No. 176 of 2018 imposes compulsory annual audited financial statements and a certified internal-control opinion irrespective of revenue or balance-sheet thresholds; no SME audit exemption exists for licensed factoring activities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); financial instruments, impairment, and derecognition of factored receivables are governed by EAS No. 49 corresponding to IFRS 9, while FRA annual returns must reconcile statutory books to IFRS treatment of sold receivables and reverse-factoring liabilities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Board of Managers must maintain the statutory UBO register and present the annual UBO confirmation to the Ordinary General Assembly that approves the annual accounts. The beneficial-ownership threshold under AML Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended, is 10% or more of shares or voting rights, direct or indirect. The annual protocol requires: (i) UBO register kept in the registered office and mapped to the ultimate parent structure; (ii) annual confirmation signed by the managers and the auditor before January 31; (iii) immediate re-confirmation upon any share transfer crossing the 10% threshold, filed with the Commercial Registry and FRA within 15 days of the reshuffle; (iv) enhanced documentary verification of the originator's ultimate beneficial holder for cross-border reverse-factoring transactions routed through escrow or Swift wire.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share ledger with transfer history)
Minute Book (general assembly and board resolutions)
UBO register per AML Law No. 80 of 2002 and FRA rule-book
Factoring client and invoices register (contracts ledger, actual and contingent receivables)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 1,800 per year for licensed corporate secretarial handling in Cairo/Giza; premium compliance agent managing UBO confirmation and FRA liaison for regulated factoring operations can reach USD 2,500 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 6,500 per year for a certified FRA-registered audit firm; a small-trade factoring portfolio below USD 500,000 of factored-book value is commonly quoted between USD 2,500 and USD 4,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying investment projects under Egypt Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 may obtain a 50% corporate income tax deduction for up to five years; free-zone companies may be subject to a 1% annual fee on value of exported products in lieu of income tax. No automatic statutory tax holiday applies to standalone trade-factoring treasury activities under ISIC 6492 unless specific Suez Canal Economic Zone regulations or FRA-licensed licensing conditions apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ETA Corporate Income Tax Return (standard juridical-person form) filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority ETA e-filing portal at www.eta.gov.eg, integrated with the official e-invoicing and e-receipt systems.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing with mandatory quarterly advance payment instalments based on estimated taxable profit; the annual return reconciles withheld taxes, instalments, loss carry-forwards, and advance credits.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than four months after the close of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, the filing and settlement deadline is 30 April of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, trade register number, Egyptian tax card number, address, and principal business activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Egyptian tax card and permanent establishment registration number of the branch/PE; do not substitute head-office identity if the PE is separately registered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the accounting period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align with the Egyptian PE statutory accounts; if head-office year differs, obtain ETA approval for the PE accounting period before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Egyptian-source revenue, including factoring commissions, reverse-factoring service fees, discount income, and ancillary supply-chain finance fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egypt-source revenue economically attributable to the PE; cross-border fee allocation must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct and overhead costs incurred in generating revenue: personnel, rent, bank charges, provision for bad debts, funding costs, and licensed IT systems.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only PE-attributable expenses evidenced by original invoices, contracts, and proof of payment; intercompany charges must satisfy arm's length standards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back fines, tax penalties, gifts, excessive management fees, non-documented cross-border invoices, and tax-depreciation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transfer pricing upward adjustments, thin-capitalisation interest disallowances, and any costs not supported by valid Egyptian e-invoices or commercial documents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward from prior years and utilised against current taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred by the Egyptian PE and within the five-year statutory carry-forward period may be utilised; losses of foreign head-office branches cannot be set off in Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit multiplied by the 22.5% corporate tax rate, reduced by foreign tax credits, advance instalments, and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard 22.5% rate to PE taxable profit; no consolidation with the parent company; attach a schedule of PE-level advance payments and any treaty-based credit claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax amount due or refund claimed after all offsets, and the bank receipt number for any accompanying payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remit the net amount in EGP through an Egyptian bank account registered with the ETA; input the relevant wire or cash deposit reference before submission.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or delayed payment triggers a monthly surcharge of 2% of the tax due for each commenced month or part thereof, plus statutory late payment interest; deliberately submitting a false return may lead to criminal prosecution, fines up to twice the tax avoided, confiscation of assets, and imprisonment. The ETA may also issue automated risk-based assessments and freeze bank accounts where e-invoicing revenue mismatches are detected.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced under an applicable double tax agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must submit an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) for the relevant year, a signed beneficial ownership declaration, and an ETA DTA-Relief application form to the Egyptian withholding agent before the distribution date. The Egyptian payer must retain the TRC and the completed application as supporting documentation to apply the reduced treaty rate; if excess withholding has already occurred, the shareholder may file a claim with the ETA for refund, subject to the statutory limitation period and substantive economic substance review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax is 20% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Under many Egyptian DTAs, the rates may be reduced to 10% for interest and 10%-15% for royalties depending on beneficial ownership and treaty terms. For factoring transactions, the discount element and implicit interest embedded in receivable purchase pricing are generally treated as interest; collection, guarantee, and service fees may be treated as technical/service fees subject to 20% statutory withholding unless a treaty alters the characterisation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where aggregate annual related-party controlled transactions exceed EGP 10 million; Master File is required where the worldwide group's annual consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 30 million. Country-by-Country reporting obligations apply to multinational groups with consolidated revenue exceeding EGP 19 billion, aligned with the OECD BEPS thresholds as adopted by Egyptian law.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not issue ESR-style declarations as in the Gulf free zones, but the ETA applies the Egyptian GAAR, anti-tax-avoidance provisions, and transfer pricing rules to require genuine economic substance. A trade supply-chain factoring LLC must maintain a physical office in Egypt, full-time commercial and risk staff, active EGP-denominated bank accounts, board decisions in Egypt, and real commercial control over receivables, credit underwriting, and collections. A letter-box entity will be challenged, treaty benefits can be denied, and restructuring may be disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of factoring income in the Egyptian corporate tax return by diverting or structuring escrow and SWIFT payment flows through unauthorised offshore accounts, tampering with e-invoices, or issuing sham receivables documents that mischaracterise taxable discount income as non-taxable trade proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, intentional tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment, a criminal fine equal to the tax evaded or twice the amount at risk, and full civil recovery of the tax deficiency plus a 2% monthly late surcharge. The ETA may also blacklist the entity, revoke tax registration, and seize bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who sign or authorise false filings may be held personally and jointly liable for the entire tax debt; Egyptian courts may order asset freezes, travel bans, and attachment of personal bank accounts; criminal conviction can result in disqualification from managing Egyptian companies for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of the Egyptian LLC as a pass-through collecting factoring fees while all negotiations, credit-risk decisions, cash management, governance, and board meetings occur outside Egypt and the LLC has no employees, no premise, no separate bank mandate, and no real risk-bearing capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may disregard the corporate entity under the General Anti-Avoidance Rules and tax the full remote-controlled income at 22.5%; all intercompany deductions may be denied; commercial registration may be cancelled under Egyptian Companies Law, and fines of up to EGP 2,000,000 may be imposed for false declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced, making shareholders and shadow directors personally liable for the corporate tax liability; travel bans and freezing of personal assets are commonly ordered where tax is at risk; individuals may also be banned from serving as directors of any Egyptian entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in recurring receivables factoring and reverse-factoring activities in Egypt without the required license from the Financial Regulatory Authority or Central Bank of Egypt, and using unregistered payment rails or escrow arrangements that do not comply with Egyptian AML/CFT record-keeping and customer-due-diligence rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed trade-finance activities attract confiscation of financial proceeds, suspension of bank accounts, and fines ranging from EGP 100,000 to EGP 2,000,000 under Egyptian AML Law No. 80 of 2002 and applicable banking/FRA regulations; senior management may face criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners engaged in AML-CFT violations face imprisonment from 3 to 7 years, travel bans, asset freezing, and forfeiture of unexplained wealth; they may also be barred from holding any position in regulated financial institutions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting cross-border factoring margins substantially below arm's length, assigning purchased receivables to a foreign entity at par without transferring risk or capital, or failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File / Master File despite related-party transaction values exceeding the ETA thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA will assess an upward transfer-pricing adjustment at 22.5% corporate income tax, plus a 2% monthly delay surcharge and interest; failure to document controlled transactions may trigger additional penalties under the ETA Transfer Pricing Guidelines and the scope of tax assessments is extended through the statutory open years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's-length arrangements without documentary support can be held personally liable for the primary tax and interest resulting from the adjustment; courts may order recovery of shifted profits, impose travel bans, and require personal restitution where the transfer was knowingly artificial.
